v.rationale: impl-1 has a real requirement bug. Its write-ability check is in the controller and runs after FormRequest validation, so a read-only token gets 422 instead of 403 for bad payloads and can probe reference uniqueness. It also answers 403 vs 404 depending on whether an order exists. impl-2 returns the right status in every case I probed because the abilities middleware runs first and lookups go through the owner's own orders. Its weaknesses are a missing integer cast (the 201 response can echo total_cents as a string), a lookup that skips route-model binding, and a few weak tests. impl-3 is the most idiomatic: abilities middleware plus a can:view policy with denyAsNotFound, a cast and an index, and the strongest Pest suite. Its only flaw is a minor 403/404 inconsistency for a token without orders:read, because the route binding resolves before the ability check (impl-1 has the same flaw). Ranking: impl-3 > impl-2 > impl-1.
